findings.description: Critical: Design D7 and tasks 2.1/2.2 project `pending_gates[]` entries with `decision_id` through `cycle_state.write_mirror`, but `skills/supervise/scripts/cycle_state.py` `_clean_pending_gate` (used by every `write_mirror` / `build_supervisor_record` path) builds a new dict that keeps only `gate`, `change_id`, `requested_at`, `deadline`, optional `disposition`/`approval_id`, and `source` — it never copies `decision_id`. Task 1.3 grows the schemas to allow `decision_id`, and task 2.8 only swaps `_GATES`/`_DISPOSITIONS` imports; no task updates the cleaner. After D7 lands, schema-valid router projections are silently stripped on write, so scenario "Router projects gate state into the mirror" and keyed re-surface by `decision_id` cannot hold.
findings.resolution: Add an explicit task (before or inside 2.2) that extends `_clean_pending_gate` to pass through `decision_id` when present, and pin it in `test_cycle_state.py` / projection tests so a round-trip through `write_mirror` preserves the field.

findings.description: Critical: Task sequencing leaves D7 projection red after its own implement step. Task 2.2 implements evaluate/answer/projection via `write_mirror` while `_GATES` is still the eight-literal frozenset in `cycle_state.py`; `roadmap_approval` is only added when task 2.8 later imports `Gate`. Until then `_clean_pending_gate` returns `None` for `gate: roadmap_approval`, so blocked roadmap approvals are dropped from the mirror even if `decision_id` were preserved. Task 2.1's projection assertions therefore cannot go green at 2.2.
findings.resolution: Move the `_GATES`/`_DISPOSITIONS` import from `shared.trust_posture` (and the `_clean_pending_gate` `decision_id` passthrough) ahead of or into task 2.2, and list `cycle_state.py` in that task's Files so projection tests can pass in the same commit as the router.

findings.description: Critical: `ApprovalGate.check_filed(gate, approval_id)` is specified to map `expired` exactly like `_interpret_status`, which calls `_apply_default(..., notified=...)`. During `evaluate`, `notified` is the real push result; on a later cycle `check_filed` has no delivery bit. With today's `BridgeCoordinatorClient.push_notification` always returning `False`, a `notify_with_timeout` + `default_action: proceed` gate fail-closes to `timeout_default_block` and stores `approval_id`. If a later `gate-check` hits D4 step 0.3 and the coordinator reports `expired`, a `check_filed` that defaults `notified=True` can apply `proceed` and unpark work nobody was notified about — bypassing the fail-closed rule `approval_gate.py` documents.
findings.resolution: Specify that `check_filed` must not re-apply a proceed default without proof of delivery: e.g. treat `expired` as non-decision (`None`) and fall through to a fresh evaluate, or require the prior ledger record's resolution/`default_action` and never upgrade an undelivered fail-closed block to proceed. Add a regression test for undelivered + expired.

findings.description: Nit: D2/D7 have `gate_router` call `cycle_state.write_mirror`, while tasks 2.7–2.9 have `cycle_state` `gate-check`/`gate-answer` call the router. Both modules would need top-level imports of each other; `cycle_state.py` already runs heavy import-time setup (`_load_runtime_models`). The plan never specifies lazy imports or a third module, so the obvious implementation risks an import cycle.
findings.resolution: Either lazy-import inside the call sites (`gate_router` imports `write_mirror` only inside the project helper; `cycle_state` imports `gate_router` only inside subcommand handlers), or move mirror projection into `cycle_state` and have the router return the pending/standing deltas for the CLI to persist.

findings.description: Nit: ADDED scenario "Router is the only seam" requires an AST scan where `.evaluate(` appears only in `gate_router.py`. If `cycle_state.py` implements `gate-check` as `gate_router.evaluate(...)` (the natural call), that attribute access matches `.evaluate(` and fails the scenario even though the seam is correct.
findings.resolution: Narrow the AST forbid list to `ApprovalGate(...).evaluate` / `evaluator.evaluate` / `build_default_gate` usage, or require `from gate_router import evaluate` (bare call) in `cycle_state` and state that explicitly in D2 and task 2.1.

findings.description: Nit: Design D2 and tasks 1.3/2.1 require gate-decision records to carry `verb` (`cycle` / `execute` / `resume`), but the change contract `contracts/schemas/gate-decision.schema.json` and the ADDED Supervise Gate Routing requirement list `decision_id`/`source`/correlation ids and omit `verb`. Records remain schema-valid via `additionalProperties: true`, so implementers and tests can disagree on whether `verb` is required.
findings.resolution: Declare optional `verb` with its enum in the change `gate-decision` schema and mention it in the ADDED requirement, or remove `verb` from D2/tasks if it is not part of the contract.

findings.description: Nit: ADDED Supervise Gate Routing opens with "SHALL append a gate-decision… record … before acting on the decision", but the prior-record rule and scenarios "Approved roadmap is not re-asked…" / re-surface paths require appending nothing. The scenarios are clear; the absolute SHALL is not.
findings.resolution: Reword to: when producing a new decision, append before acting; reuse and unchanged re-surface append nothing and leave the mirror untouched.

findings.description: Nit: D5 says exit codes "mirror `runner.py gate-check`" yet redefine exit 4: runner's `EXIT_GATE_PARKED` means no console question remains (ESCALATE; `gate-answer` has nothing pending), while supervise exit 4 still keeps a `pending_gates` entry and explicitly allows `gate-answer`. Hosts or operators who reuse runner semantics will treat exit 4 as unanswerable.
findings.resolution: Drop the "mirror" claim and document the deliberate divergence (0 = askable posture_block, 3 = proceed, 4 = terminal block that remains answerable via supervise `gate-answer`), or align exit 4 with runner and use another code for answerable terminal blocks.

findings.description: Optional: D7 sets `change_id` on a `roadmap_approval` `pending_gates` entry to "the roadmap's first ready item's change" because `pendingGate` requires `change_id`. A roadmap with no ready item (or no `change_id`s yet) has no value that satisfies the schema, so `write_mirror` validation would reject the projection and the gate could not be surfaced.
findings.resolution: Define a stable fallback (e.g. a sentinel tied to `roadmap_id`, or relax `change_id` when `gate` is `roadmap_approval`) and add a test for an empty/not-yet-scaffolded roadmap.

findings.description: FYI: wp-contracts `write_allow` includes `skills/tests/supervise/test_supervisor_record_schema.py` (task 1.1), but package verification only runs `skills/shared/tests` and selected autopilot gate tests — not that supervise schema file. A broken nine-gate schema assertion there is only caught after wp-router's full supervise suite.
findings.resolution: Add `skills/.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/tests/supervise/test_supervisor_record_schema.py -q` to wp-contracts verification, or move that test edit into wp-router.

findings.description: The plan correctly grounds the prior-record / `check_filed` design in real gate-service behaviour: `ApprovalGate.evaluate` is synchronous and never returns pending under `notify_with_timeout`, and `build_gate_request` is only used for `posture_block` and never carries `approval_id`. That avoids re-implementing notify polling in the router.
findings.resolution: Keep D4's ledger-first rule; fix the `expired`/`notified` gap in finding 3 without reintroducing an async pending path.

findings.description: MODIFIED OpenSpec requirements reproduce every live scenario (often strengthened), and wp-router ∥ wp-skill-docs keep non-overlapping write scopes (`scripts/**` vs `SKILL.md` / prose tests) with skill-docs denying `scripts/**` and router denying `SKILL.md`, so the parallel cut is sound once the `_clean_pending_gate` sequencing gap is fixed.
findings.resolution: No change to the package DAG; land findings 1–2 inside wp-router before treating projection as done.
